newsitem.title: TANZANIA: South Africa team in Tanzania talks on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: South Africa team in Tanzania talks on Zaire.

text.p: A South African delegation including senior military officers discussed on Thursday in Tanzania how Pretoria could contribute to ending the disaster in Zaire.

"It's an exploratory visit, a consultative visit to a region ...very close to the problem," said Welile Nhlapo, South African ambassador to the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) and special envoy on Burundi.

He told Reuters the two-day visit by the South African team, which arrived on Thursday, was in response to former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere's asking for South African participation in a multinational force for east Zaire.
Asked if the lack of a political solution posed special risks to any foreign force, Nhlapo said: "That's part of what we're exploring. The problem is the nature of the operation."
He said South Africa was involved in numerous consultations with partners in Africa before making any firm commitment to join a force for Central Africa and much work needed to be done.
The team met Nyerere in Dar es Salaam and was briefed by Tanzanian Foreign Ministry officials.
"They should be participating in events in Africa," said Nyerere's spokesman Charles Sanga. "They are part of us now and they should be involved in what we're doing."

"It's a first, very hesitant and investigative step from South Africa before involvement in the region. It's definitely not a military planning exercise," said South African Colonel Tienie van Schalkwyk.
Mandela said on Wednesday the South African team would consider military questions and political solutions to the crisis and find out exactly what was required of South Africa.
Schalkwyk said the team was led by Rusty Evans, Foreign Ministry director-general, and included three senior military officers.
The top officer is Lieutenant-General Wessel Kritzinger, chief of staff for defence operations.

Schalkwyk said it was unlikely South Africa would commit combat troops but would rather play a key supporting role possibly involved in logistics, communications, field engineers or the medical field.
